answer: One concrete defense is costly staking: each agent must bond scarce collateral to claim a seat, so spinning up a thousand clones burns real value instead of being free. An honest identity becomes a pearl worth protecting, while every cheap sybil is an ember that gutters out under slashing. Reputation then bends like a willow, flexible but rooted, accruing slowly to agents that stake and behave rather than to disposable fakes.
